disclaimer: Advisory only. Confirm with your local agriculture officer / KVK and follow the product label.

rules.headline: Pest population low and canopy healthy
actions: Maintain routine weekly scouting across 5 plants x 3 canopy levels (top, middle, bottom leaves).
Conserve natural bio-control agents: Ladybird beetles (Coccinellids), Green Lacewings (Chrysoperla zastrowi), and predatory spiders.
Maintain balanced soil nutrition; avoid excess urea/nitrogen top-dressing which stimulates succulent vegetative growth.
Eradicate alternate host weeds (e.g., Abutilon indicum, Parthenium) along field borders.
rules.spray_guidance: No chemical intervention warranted. Economic threshold level has not been reached.

rules.headline: Residual leaf symptoms observed despite low pest count
actions: Re-inspect foliage in 5 days to confirm whether hopper burn is residual from a previous generation or secondary stress.
Check leaf underside closely for emerging first-instar translucent nymphs along veins.
Ensure adequate soil moisture to relieve physiological leaf edge scorching.
rules.spray_guidance: Hold chemical spray; evaluate if hopper burn is stabilized or expanding.

rules.headline: Effective suppression maintained by recent treatment
actions: Previous spray is actively suppressing jassid population within expected residual window.
Monitor underside for surviving nymph hot-spots; avoid unnecessary repeat spray to conserve natural enemies.
Next field scout scheduled in 7 days.
rules.spray_guidance: Do not repeat spray; allow residual window to protect beneficial predatory fauna.

rules.headline: Moderate pest density approaching economic threshold
actions: Re-scout field in 4 days. Sample at least 15 leaves to verify population trajectory.
Install yellow sticky traps (5-10 traps per acre) at crop canopy level to monitor adult leafhopper flight.
Eliminate alternate host weed reservoirs surrounding the field margins (Okra, Brinjal, and wild mallows).
Prepare botanical bio-pesticide option (Neem Oil 1500 ppm or 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract).
rules.spray_guidance: Consider bio-pesticide (Neem formulation 1500 ppm / Azadirachtin) or bio-agent release (Chrysoperla zastrowi) if count crosses 1.5 per leaf.

rules.headline: Noticeable leaf margin injury and growing nymph counts
actions: Re-scout within 3 days. Early upward leaf cupping indicates active phloem feeding.
Avoid any supplemental nitrogenous fertilizers; promote potassium / foliar micronutrients to support leaf recovery.
Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or State Agricultural Extension officer for locally approved IPM products.
rules.spray_guidance: If counts reach 2 jassids/leaf upon next scout, plan targeted intervention using an appropriate chemical class. Rotate class if previously sprayed.

rules.headline: Moderate pest count detected within post-spray window
actions: Re-evaluate efficacy of the applied product. Check for pesticide rain wash-off or improper spray coverage under leaves.
Ensure full canopy underside penetration in any subsequent application.
Check for presence of nymphal stages vs migrating adults from neighboring fields.
rules.spray_guidance: If re-treatment is needed after residual period ends, rotate to an alternate IRAC mode of action class (never reuse same class back-to-back).

rules.headline: Pest population has breached Economic Threshold Level (ETL)
actions: Immediate intervention warranted: jassid density exceeds ETL (>= 2 nymphs/leaf or >= 6 per 3 leaves).
Calibrate spray equipment (hollow cone nozzle) to thoroughly target the underside of the canopy.
Re-scout 2-3 days post-treatment to verify knock-down efficacy.
Withhold nitrogen application until pest pressure is subdued.
rules.spray_guidance: Select an approved sucking pest insecticide from a fresh chemical class (e.g. Neonicotinoid or Organophosphate if not sprayed recently). Follow label directions.

rules.headline: Severe pest outbreak with widespread hopper burn injury
actions: Urgent action required: High pest count combined with severe Grade 2+ leafhopper burn cupping/scorching.
Risk of premature boll drop, stunted vegetative growth, and significant yield loss.
Spray without delay during early morning or evening hours with proper personal protective equipment (PPE).
Inspect adjoining fields (especially okra/eggplant) for incoming pest swarms.
rules.spray_guidance: Apply recommended systemic / contact insecticide class per ICAR/TNAU guidelines. Rotate IRAC group from prior sprays to prevent resistance.

rules.headline: High pest pressure persists despite recent spray
actions: Investigate spray failure causes: heavy rainfall wash-off, degraded product, inadequate water volume (use 200 L/acre), or development of insecticide resistance.
Strictly rotate to a completely different chemical class (e.g., if Neonicotinoid was used, switch to Flonicamid, Diafenthiuron, or Organophosphate as advised by KVK).
Report persistent control failure to local Agricultural Officer.
rules.spray_guidance: Do not repeat the same chemical class. Consult KVK for resistance-breaking IPM rotation.
